# Brass and metallic zinc (`zinc_brass`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/materials.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Metallurgy & materials (`materials`)
- Deps: needs copper_bronze; helped by refractories_fireclay, distillation
- Core idea: Zinc boils at 907 °C, below the temperature at which charcoal reduces its ore, so in an ordinary furnace it leaves as vapour and burns to white smoke. Brass is therefore made without ever seeing zinc: heat small pieces of copper with roasted, ground calamine (zinc ore) and charcoal in a closed crucible at about 900–950 °C for many hours, and the zinc vapour soaks into the copper up to about 28–30 %; then raise the heat to melt and pour. To win the metal itself, heat the ore and charcoal in sealed clay retorts whose necks point downward into a cooler chamber, where the vapour condenses to drops.
- Pitfalls:
  - Smelting zinc ore like copper or lead ore; all the metal is lost up the chimney.
  - Raising the crucible to copper's melting point too early; the zinc escapes before it is absorbed.
  - Breathing the white zinc fumes gives 'brass-founders' ague' (a day of fever and chills).
  - Confusing calamine with other white earths; test whether it turns copper golden.
  - Expecting brass to quench-harden; it hardens only by hammering.
- History: mesopotamia: 3rd–2nd millennium BC – occasional brass objects, probably accidental; 8th–7th c. BC deliberate cementation brass in Anatolia (Gordion); rome: c. 23 BC – Augustus's coinage reform uses orichalcum (brass) for sestertii and dupondii; india: c. 9th c. AD – zinc distilled by downward condensation at Zawar (Rajasthan), on an industrial scale by the 12th–16th c.; described in the Rasaratnakara and Rasarnava; china: 16th c. – zinc smelting under the Ming; exported to Europe as 'tutenag' in the 17th c.; islamic: 9th–12th c. – cementation brass (shabah) a major craft; tutty (zinc oxide) collected from furnaces; europe: medieval cementation brass at Dinant and Aachen; 1738 William Champion's patent for zinc distillation (Bristol); 1746 Marggraf describes the metal; africa: 9th–15th c. AD – leaded brass and bronze castings at Igbo-Ukwu, Ife and Benin
- Read:
  - P. T. Craddock (ed.), 2000 Years of Zinc and Brass (1990)
  - R. F. Tylecote, A History of Metallurgy (1976)
